auth.invite.expires: The link expires on {date}. You will confirm your email address with a one-time code.

auth.invite.subject: You're invited to {target}
auth.magic.code_hint: If the link opens in a different browser than the one you used, enter this code instead:

billing.past_due.action: To keep the workspace running, update the payment details or choose a plan on the billing page.
billing.past_due.deadline: Unless it is back in good standing by {deadline}, the workspace will be suspended: your team will only be able to reach the billing page, and investors will see that the portal is unavailable.
billing.past_due.intro: The subscription for {workspace} could not be paid, or it has ended.
billing.past_due.subject: Payment needed for {workspace}
billing.past_due.title: Payment needed for {workspace}
billing.suspended.effect: Owners can still sign in and open the billing page. Everything else, including the investor portal, is unavailable until the subscription is paid; the workspace then reopens by itself.
billing.suspended.intro: {workspace} has been suspended because its subscription was not paid by the end of the grace period.
billing.suspended.subject: {workspace} has been suspended
billing.suspended.title: {workspace} has been suspended
security.break_glass.audit: Every statement run in this session is recorded in your workspace's audit log (actions starting with host.break_glass). If you did not expect this, contact the operator and quote the ticket.
security.break_glass.expires: The session ends at {expires} at the latest.
security.break_glass.intro: The operator of the server that hosts your workspace opened a time-limited emergency ("break-glass") session on {workspace}. For its duration they can read your workspace's data directly in the database, past the normal access checks.
security.break_glass.subject: Security notice: operator access to {workspace}
security.break_glass.title: The operator opened emergency access to {workspace}
security.break_glass_write.audit: The statement's SHA-256 fingerprint is {sha256}; it is in your workspace's audit log. Quote it to the operator to see the statement itself.

security.break_glass_write.intro.one: In emergency session {session} (ticket {ticket}) the operator ran a {verb} statement that affected {count} row.
security.break_glass_write.intro.other: In emergency session {session} (ticket {ticket}) the operator ran a {verb} statement that affected {count} rows.

security.break_glass_write.subject: Security notice: the operator changed data in {workspace}
security.break_glass_write.title: The operator changed data in {workspace}
